Keywords: search ads match type exact phrase broad modified keyword targeting
Goal: Control which searches trigger your ads. Exact Match = precise control. Phrase Match = some flexibility. Broad Match = maximum reach (requires Smart Bidding).
Setup: Exact [keyword] — only exact searches. Phrase 'keyword' — searches containing phrase. Broad keyword — variations and related searches. Start with Exact and Phrase. Add Broad only with Smart Bidding + conversion history.
Bidding: Exact/Phrase: Manual CPC or Enhanced CPC. Broad: Target CPA or Target ROAS (Smart Bidding required for Broad match)
Budget: Allocate 70% budget to best-performing match types. Use Broad only after 30+ conversions/month.
Metrics: CTR by match type, impression share, cost per conversion, search term report quality
Do: Use negative keywords aggressively. Review Search Terms Report weekly. Start narrow (Exact), expand to Broad after optimization.
Dont: Don't use Broad Match without Smart Bidding and conversion data. Don't ignore Search Terms Report — it reveals wasted spend and new keyword opportunities.

Keywords: responsive search ads RSA headlines descriptions CTA copy quality score CTR
Goal: Responsive Search Ads (RSA) — up to 15 headlines and 4 descriptions, Google auto-tests combinations. Write diverse, non-repetitive assets.
Setup: 15 headlines: include keyword (1-3 headlines), USPs (3-4), CTAs (2-3), proof (2-3), emotional hooks (1-2). 4 descriptions: expand on benefits, include CTA. Google recommends 'Good' or 'Excellent' strength — aim for Excellent.
Bidding: Smart Bidding (tCPA or tROAS) works best with diverse RSA assets
Budget: Include keyword in Headline 1. Add price/offer if competitive. Use countdown timer for limited offers. Include CTAs ('Get a Quote', 'Start Free Trial').
Metrics: CTR (aim 3-8% for branded, 1-3% for non-branded), Ad Strength (aim Excellent), Quality Score (aim 7+)
Do: Test 2-3 RSA variations per ad group. Include emotional hooks AND rational benefits. Pin Headline 1 to keyword-focused headline.
Dont: Don't repeat the same message across all headlines. Don't skip descriptions. Don't ignore Ad Strength suggestions from Google.

Keywords: negative keywords search term wasted spend irrelevant traffic budget protection
Goal: Negative keywords prevent your ads from showing for irrelevant searches. Critical for budget efficiency. Missing negatives = wasted spend.
Setup: Weekly: Review Search Terms Report → Identify irrelevant queries → Add as negatives at ad group, campaign, or account level. Build a master negative keyword list. Add common negatives from day 1 (free, jobs, reviews, DIY, Wikipedia).
Budget: 10-20% of budget saved with proactive negative keyword management.
Metrics: Wasted spend rate, Search Terms relevance %
Do: Review Search Terms Report WEEKLY. Create negative keyword lists to apply across campaigns. Add branded terms as negatives in competitor campaigns.
Dont: Don't set and forget — negatives must be actively maintained. Don't add negative keywords before checking if they'll block important traffic (use Keyword Planner to check volume impact).

Keywords: smart bidding target cpa target roas maximize conversions automated bidding machine learning
Goal: Google's AI-powered bidding automatically sets bids to achieve your target goal. Works best with sufficient conversion data. Outperforms Manual CPC when properly set up.
Setup: Target CPA: Set desired cost per conversion. Target ROAS: Set desired return (e.g. 400% = $4 revenue per $1 spend). Maximize Conversions: no target (uses full budget). Minimum: 30 conversions/month for tCPA, 50 for tROAS.
Bidding: Switch to Smart Bidding after 30+ conversions. Start with Maximize Conversions, then add CPA/ROAS targets once Google has data.
Budget: Conversion volume, CPA vs target, ROAS vs target. Monitor weekly, not daily.
Metrics: Allow 4-6 week learning period. Don't change bids or budget drastically during learning. Set realistic targets based on historical data.
Do: Don't set a tCPA 50% lower than your historical CPA — Google won't find conversions at that level. Don't make frequent campaign changes during learning period (resets learning).

Keywords: performance max pmax all placements ai campaign google ads automation asset groups
Goal: PMax runs across all Google surfaces (Search, Display, YouTube, Shopping, Gmail, Discover, Maps) from one campaign. Replaces Smart Shopping and Local campaigns. Requires rich creative assets.
Setup: Create Asset Groups (like ad groups): 3-5 image assets (various sizes), 5 video assets (or Google creates from images), 5 headlines, 5 descriptions. Add Audience Signals. List URL rules. Connect product feed for Shopping.
Bidding: Budget: $50-200/day minimum. Bidding: Maximize Conversion Value (or set ROAS target after 30 days)
Budget: Conversion value, ROAS, new customers vs returning, asset group performance
Metrics: Give Google 4-6 weeks to learn. Add high-quality video assets (auto-created videos are low quality). Use Audience Signals to guide Google (but it can go beyond them).
Do: Don't limit URL rules too strictly (Google needs to test pages). Don't ignore Asset Group performance insights. Don't change campaign heavily in first 4 weeks (resets learning).

Keywords: google shopping merchant center product feed shopping ads e-commerce product listing ads PLA
Goal: Shopping ads show product images, prices, and titles directly in Google search results. Driven by product feed data, not keywords.
Setup: Submit product feed to Merchant Center (Google Sheets, XML feed, or e-commerce platform plugin). Optimize feed: product title (most important — include keyword), description, images (white background, 800x800px), price, GTIN.
Bidding: Standard Shopping: CPC with Manual or tROAS. Smart Shopping replaced by PMax. CSS (Comparison Shopping Service) reduces CPC in EU.
Budget: Impression share, ROAS, CTR, average CPC, conversion rate per product category
Metrics: Optimize product titles (keyword + product name + key spec). Use negative keywords aggressively. Submit promotions for promotional labels.
Do: Don't have low-quality product images (no watermarks, white background preferred). Don't ignore Merchant Center disapprovals — they stop all Shopping ads. Don't skip GTIN (Google uses it for product matching).

Keywords: display remarketing retargeting banner website visitor custom audience awareness branding
Goal: Show banner/image ads to people who previously visited your site. Keeps your brand visible during the consideration phase.
Setup: Create custom audiences from GA4 (website visitors, cart abandoners) or Google Ads audiences. Create responsive display ads: 5 images (various sizes), 5 headlines, 5 descriptions, logo. Set frequency cap (3-5 impressions/user/day).
Bidding: CPM for awareness. Target CPA for conversion-focused remarketing. Manual CPC for control.
Metrics: Frequency, viewability rate, VTC (view-through conversions), click conversion rate
Do: Set frequency caps to avoid ad fatigue (3-5 impressions/day max). Exclude converted customers. Layer timing (show different ads based on days since visit).
Dont: Don't show identical ads to all website visitors regardless of what they viewed. Don't skip frequency caps — showing ads 20x/day damages brand perception. Don't use generic banner designs — include offer or proof.

Keywords: youtube video ads TrueView skippable non-skippable in-stream bumper CPV brand awareness
Goal: Video ads on YouTube. Skippable In-Stream (TrueView): 15-30s before/during videos, pay when watched 30s+. Non-skippable: 15s, always watched. Bumper: 6s non-skippable. Discovery: thumbnail in search.
Setup: Create video in YouTube Studio. Set up campaign in Google Ads: Video campaign type → Select ad format. Add video URL. Set targeting (topics, placements, audiences, keywords). Create compelling thumbnail.
Bidding: Skippable: CPV (cost per view). Non-skippable: CPM. Bumper: CPM. Brand awareness & Reach objective for awareness.
column11: Hook in first 5 seconds (before skip button). Include brand name/logo in first 5 seconds. Add end screen CTA.
column12: Don't use long intros before the hook (user will skip). Don't use TV-style ads on YouTube without adapting for skip behavior. Don't run video ads without conversion tracking to measure downstream impact.

Keywords: ga4 google ads conversion import link connect share attribution measurement
Goal: Import GA4 key events directly into Google Ads as conversions. More accurate than the Google Ads tag alone, uses GA4 attribution. Required for Smart Bidding optimization.
Setup: In GA4: Admin → Google Ads Links → Create Link. In Google Ads: Tools → Conversions → Import → Google Analytics 4 → Select property → Import key events as conversions.
Bidding: N/A — affects all Smart Bidding campaigns
Budget: Better attribution, more accurate ROAS, unlocks GA4 audience targeting in Google Ads.
Metrics: Accurate conversions in Google Ads, match rate between GA4 and Ads
Do: Use GA4 import as PRIMARY conversion source. Pause Google Ads conversion tags (avoid double counting). This enables model-based conversions for iOS/Consent Mode.
Dont: Don't import AND keep the Google Ads conversion tag active (double counts). Don't import ALL GA4 events — only meaningful business conversions. Don't skip the Google Ads ↔ GA4 link.
